newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber extends gains at close on covering.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber extends gains at close on covering.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended higher on late short-covering for SMR grades after a steady opening, traders said.

At the close, the benchmark September RSS1 buyer was quoted at 330 cents ($1.32) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, up 0.50 cent from Thursday's close. September SMR20 buyer was 1.5 cents higher at 314 ($1.26) cents a kg.

Trading houses also offered the SMR20 at 312 cents but perked prices of other grades slightly. SMR10 was offered at 314, SMR5 at 326 and SMR L at 357. September/October SMR CV and drum latex were quoted at 377-378 and 248, respectively.
Trading was restrained in the morning but picked up in the afternoon on short-covering, particularly for the SMR L. "The mixed to bearish trends in Japan were not a factor today," said a dealer.
Traders said producers were slightly reserved in selling after rains reduced tapping activities and tightened supply of raw materials into the market this week.
The INRO five-day average rose to 247.90 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Aug 29 from 246.74 on Aug 28. The daily indicator rose to 250.80 from 249.78.
